clue.text: Vessel — cooks with it

parts.note: to cook food over boiling water is to steam it; 'cooks' is the verb
hip means fashionable, up to date, with it

explanation.surface: A remark about kitchen staff bringing something along with them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' looks like a pot the cooks use, but it is a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship driven by steam power is a kind of seagoing vessel.

clue.text: Loose stones on church yard, originally making harsh noise

parts.note: scree is a mass of loose stones on a slope

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Stones scattered across a churchyard once made a grating sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'church yard' reads as churchyard but splits: CH, then Y from 'yard, originally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something giving a shrill, grating cry is screeching or harsh-sounding.

clue.text: Male or female writer causing upset to the cloth

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: toile is a linen or cotton cloth

explanation.surface: A writer annoys the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the cloth' suggests the clergy, but it is fabric. George Eliot was a woman writing under a man's name, hence 'Male or female'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mary Ann Evans wrote as George, a female novelist with a male pen name; T.S. was the male poet.

clue.text: It's an omen, unfortunately, for St. Paul's state

indicators.note: an unfortunate turn of events messes things up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored, leaving the letters I, T, S

explanation.surface: A bad sign for the cathedral or the apostle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'St. Paul' suggests the London cathedral; it is the capital city of a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Paul is the capital city of this midwestern American state.

clue.text: Spoken acknowledgement of girl's healthy practices

indicators.note: the words are said out loud, so their sound is what counts

parts.note: a greeting to a girl, 'Hi, Jean'

explanation.surface: A girl's verbal thanks for good health habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acknowledgement' is the greeting HI and 'girl' is JEAN; said together they give the answer; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleanliness habits that keep people well are good sanitary practice.

clue.text: Botanist's initial fuss over this plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the fuss sits above the letter

parts.note: pother is an old word for fuss or commotion

indicators.note: an initial is a first letter

explanation.surface: A botanist starts making a fuss about this plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot-herb is a leafy vegetable or culinary herb grown for cooking.

clue.text: Animal making escape in city in US

indicators.note: the escape word is placed inside the city abbreviation

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
lam is slang for a hasty escape, as in 'on the lam'

explanation.surface: A creature breaks loose somewhere in an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American beast of burden is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Tool of revolution, producing endless agitation

indicators.note: without its end means the final letter is removed

parts.note: a lather is a state of agitation, as in getting into a lather

explanation.surface: Revolutionaries' weapon causing constant unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests uprising; here it means rotating, since this machine spins the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that spins a workpiece against a cutter is a tool that works by rotation.

clue.text: A universal cheese — one consumed by volunteers in plant

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal
brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: consumed means eaten up, so one letter goes inside the other piece

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Soldier volunteers eat a cheese among the flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A trailing purple-flowered rock plant, often spelt aubrietia, is a garden plant.

clue.text: Out of bed and not at home, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so a soundalike is wanted

parts.note: away means not at home

explanation.surface: Someone is up and has gone out, so we're told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of bed' looks like getting up; it is an anchor raised clear of the sea bed.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor just lifted off the sea floor is said to be clear of the bottom.

clue.text: As a rule, sound made by cats and dogs

indicators.note: the word is heard spoken, so a soundalike is wanted

parts.note: raining cats and dogs means heavy rain, so the phrase stands for rain

explanation.surface: Generally speaking, pets are noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As a' is link; 'cats and dogs' is the idiom for heavy downpour, not the animals' noises.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's period of rule over a country is their reign.

clue.text: Understand a display of data readily at hand

parts.note: to get something is to understand it
a table lays data out in rows and columns

explanation.surface: Grasping a chart of figures that is close by.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obtainable, easy to reach, is readily at hand.

clue.text: Former part of army taking troop leader over the top.

indicators.note: the combined letters take in, or hold, another letter

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a corps of the British Army

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An ex-soldier leading the troops charging over the top of the trench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over the top' pictures soldiers leaving the trenches; here it means excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive or far beyond reasonable limits is the idiomatic sense of over the top.

clue.text: Establishing equality late in the day

definitions.meaning: making things level or equal, the verb form of making even
the part of the day after afternoon, before night

explanation.definitionFit: One word is both the participle of levelling things and the noun for the day's end.

clue.text: Wait expectantly, without inspiration?

definitions.meaning: to wait in suspense for something to happen
inspiration read literally as breathing in, so not inhaling at all

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for anxious waiting also literally means stopping inhaling, the physical sense of inspiration.

clue.text: Not sufficiently motivated to permit husband special cigar

parts.note: to let is to permit

indicators.note: special suggests a version made differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Too lazy to let a husband have a fancy cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: Sluggish and lacking energy, someone lethargic cannot rouse themselves.

clue.text: Good try, Morse!

definitions.meaning: Inspector Morse's rarely used first name in Colin Dexter's novels

explanation.definitionFit: The word for an earnest attempt is also the first name of the fictional Oxford detective Morse.

clue.text: Gut reaction perceptible this month in court

annotationWithheld.why: Gut reaction perceptible this month in court (8): INST + IN + CT gives every letter, leaving 'perceptible' with no job and no source explaining it
annotationWithheld.clue: Gut reaction perceptible this month in court

clue.text: Gangs traded war spoils in bitter enmity

indicators.note: to spoil the words is to ruin their order, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rival gangs share out the plunder from their feud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoils' reads as the noun for plunder but is a verb signalling an anagram of GANGS TRADED WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes two parties openly hostile, ready to fight, with blades unsheathed.

clue.text: Old woman making a lot of money before midday

parts.note: a grand is a thousand pounds or dollars
am is ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: A woman earns a fortune in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a grandmother or old lady.

clue.text: Chairs meeting — not quiet at first, but settles

indicators.note: not means the quiet letter is left out
the omitted letter sits at the start

parts.note: someone who chairs a meeting presides over it
p, piano, means quiet in music

explanation.surface: A chairman runs a noisy meeting before calming it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chairs' looks like furniture but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle somewhere is to make one's home, to live there.

clue.text: Big cat gives us shock, catching fever out East

indicators.note: one piece catches, holds, another inside it

parts.note: a jar is a jolt or shock

indicators.note: out means the letter for East is removed

parts.note: ague is a malarial fever
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A big cat startles us when we fall sick in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: The large spotted American wild cat is an example of a big cat.

clue.text: A graduate with a research position initially in southern state

parts.note: a lab, laboratory, is where research takes place
a lab, laboratory, is where research takes place
MA is Master of Arts, a graduate
MA is Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate takes up a research post in a state in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' moves the research post ahead of the graduate in the answer, against the clue's order; 'with' and 'in' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The US state on the Gulf of Mexico is one of the Deep South states.

clue.text: Some saw a representative knowing about current developments

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few people saw a delegate who keeps up with the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Being informed or well up on events means being clued up on what is happening.

clue.text: Archangel, for example, English pastor's confused about

indicators.note: a confused mind is muddled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter

explanation.surface: An English pastor is muddled about the archangels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Archangel' suggests Gabriel or Michael, but it is Arkhangelsk, a Russian port city on the White Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Arkhangelsk, called Archangel in English, is a harbour town on Russia's northern coast.

clue.text: Round small islands going North to old Italian port

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means read upwards

parts.note: aits are small islands in a river

explanation.surface: A voyage round little islands, heading north to an old harbour in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient harbour town at the mouth of the Tiber served Rome as its port.

clue.text: Careless and open to attack

definitions.meaning: incautious, speaking without thinking, as in an incautious moment

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both incautious in speech and literally left without protection.

clue.text: It's not infrequently decimal

definitions.meaning: read as two words, decimal means based on, or made ...

explanation.definitionFit: The adverb for many times, split into two words, describes a decimal system.

clue.text: Lacy frill male dog rejected 'at first

indicators.note: the turned dog comes at the start, before the male
rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A frilly item was turned down by a male dog first.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathered strip of fabric used as a trimming is a kind of lace-like frill.

clue.text: A lot of nasty crime could come from him

definitions.text: A lot of nasty crime could come from him

indicators.note: the letters could be shaped into something new, so they are rearranged
a lot of a word is most of it, here less its final letter

explanation.surface: Lots of nasty wrongdoing is the work of a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' drops the Y of NASTY, giving NAST; with CRIME that is rearranged by 'could come from'. The whole clue also describes a villain.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer or villain is the person who would commit such nasty crime.
